key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 treatment initially reduces interfacial recombination but accelerates degradation under thermal aging, with losses extending into the perovskite bulk.
engineering_relevance: Nondestructive, depth-sensitive monitoring can help engineers distinguish initial interface-passivation benefits from long-term thermal-stability trade-offs in perovskite solar cells.
method: Use multiple excitation wavelengths to probe interface- and bulk-dominated photoluminescence responses.
Track recombination changes in PEABF4-treated perovskite stacks during thermal aging.
Interpret decay signatures using diffusion–recombination simulations.
evidence_signal: PL measurements indicate reduced recombination losses from fullerene deposition after treatment, followed by faster thermal degradation; simulations support interpreting the wavelength-dependent signatures through surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime changes.
watch_item: Depth localization is model-supported rather than direct imaging, and the abstract provides no quantitative degradation rates or device-lifetime validation.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
